full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J : The defendant-petitioners filed an application for recording an order of abatement in Civil Revision NO.718 of 1988, which was finally disposed of by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division on 9-11-94. The learned Single Judge rejected the application. Hence, the defendant-petitioners filed this petition for leave to appeal against the defendant-petitioners. Suit was decreed by the trial Court. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendant-petitioners preferred Title Appeal No.78 of 1986 and the same was allowed by the Subordinate Judge, Shariatpur and the suit was dismissed. Against that judgment and decree the plaintiff-respondents preferred Civil Revision No.718 of 1988. In the said civil revision there was no appearance on behalf of the present petitioners. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute after setting aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court and restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court passed in the said partition suit in preliminary form in favour of the plaintiff-respondents. After disposal of the civil revision on 9-11-94, the defendant-petitioners filed this application for recording an order of abatement and by an order dated 7th July, 1996 the said application was rejected. 

 2. The civil revision case having been disposed of two years back the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division held that this application was filed for recording an order of abatement only to delay the drawing up of the final decree in the partition suit. Particularly, the civil revision case having been disposed of' two years back there remains nothing for recording an order of abatement in the case which was disposed of on merit by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division. The discretion having been exercised judiciously there is nothing for our interference.
